findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A partially used gallon of milk was observed in the front area standing cooler with a date placed on it of 8/25. This was a date 10 days prior to the date of observation. When discussed, the PIC indicated that the observed date was the day that the milk was brought into the facility and that the container had only been opened the Tuesday prior (four days prior to the inspection). Education was conducted. The date needed for seven day date marking is the day in which the container was opened. If there are other policies in play at the facility level this is acceptable, but they must be in addition to the seven day date marking required by the code. A date was added for Tuesday to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the date marking policies include those required by the code in the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

On arrival several cases of to-go containers were observed on the floor in the back of the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC a they were instructed to stored these items off of the floor (at least six inches) prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that hand washing is reviewed and all employees are sufficiently trainings to wash their hands correctly at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the front of the facility would not register on the inspector test strips. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A gallon of milk is observed in the front standing cooler partially used and without a date marking. A conversation with the PIC indicated that the milk had not been used so far today, indicating that it was opened yesterday at best. Education was conducted and a date marking added to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A rag is observed moist and laying on a counter on the in the front prep area. This rag is used for wiping food contact surfaces and should be stored between uses in a sanitizer solution. The PIC was shown and the rag moved to a fresh sani bucket to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The only test strips available in the facility during this inspection are for a quat based sanitizer. The only sanitizer currently being used in the facility is CL based (bleach). The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have test strips that match their sanitizing chemicals at all times. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival there was not a CFPM available on site. The CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct. Ensure that there is a CFPM on site at all times that food handling/preparation activities are happening.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the sani bucket in the front of the facility would not register on the inspector’s test strips. The bucket was remade during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the in use sanitizers are at effective concentrations at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. 

A partially used gallon of milk in a standing cooler is observed with a date marking of 8/24. This makes today day #11 since opening when the item should have been used or discarded by the end of day #7. Education was conducted and the container discarded to correct. Ensure that date marking practices are followed for all RTE (Ready to Eat) TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods in the facility.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

The bleach currently being used in the facility does not meet regulatory requirements. The bottles are lemon scented, do not have an EPA Registration number and do not have instructions for intended uses related to food contact surfaces. Education was conducted and a new bottle will need to be acquired. Per CK, inspector will spot check tomorrow for compliance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

The test strips available in the facility are intended for a Quat based sanitizer while the facility is using a CL based sanitizer (bleach). Education was conducted and a small amount of test strips acquired during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the test strips available are intended for the chemicals used by the facility.
